title: vela-payments-prospect-playbook-notes
body:
Notes to self — Vela Payments (mid-market PSP) prospect playbook.

Quick thesis: Vela has a merchant platform (SaaS + PSP) that could use an LLM layer across: dispute triage, merchant support routing, automated reconciliation notes, and fraud signal enrichment. If we can pitch a low-risk pilot that reduces average handle time for merchant support AND shows token-cost per case savings vs current fine-tuned API calls, they'll be interested.

Target personas (map + outreach order):
- Head of Product (payments platform) — primary economic buyer for platform-level integration.
- Director, Risk & Fraud — cares about signal enrichment + latency for fraud score updates.
- VP, Merchant Ops / Support — will own pilot for AHT reduction.
- Platform / SRE lead — will ask private deployment / VPC / latency questions.

Key value props to lean on:
- Predictable cost at production scale (Redwood Dedicated): reserve pool reduces per-token variance vs public cloud bursts.
- Low-latency inference for near-real-time fraud decisions (latency SLO, KV caching).
- Data isolation + compliance (Private/VPC option + KMS support).
- Rollouts & fallback: can A/B a model and fall back to smaller variant when traffic spikes.

Cold outreach skeleton (short, 2-stager):
Email 1 subject: "Pilot to cut merchant support AHT by 25% — Vela + Redwood?"
Body highlights: 1) quick hook (we helped a PSP cut avg case token count by 38%), 2) concrete pilot ask (2-week pilot on 500 ticket samples; Redwood handles hosting and SOC controls), 3) CTA (15-min sync).
Email 2 (if no reply): short social proof + 1-pager attached 
LinkedIn note: reference mutual investor or API partner; ask for intro to VP Merchant Ops.

Discovery question bank (for initial 15–30m):
- Walk me through a recent merchant support case end-to-end — where are the pain points?
- Volume: daily ticket count, average chars/token length of messages, peak concurrency windows.
- What systems store case metadata? (Zendesk/Intercom + internal DBs?)
- Current tooling: any LLMs or heuristic automations in use? cost per inference?
- Compliance/regulatory constraints on merchant/customer data? retention windows?
- Who would sign off on a pilot (security, legal, platform)?
- Success metrics: AHT reduction, intent accuracy, false positive rate, cost per resolved case.

Pilot blueprint (2 weeks) — low-friction, measurable:
- Week 0: ingest 500 anonymized ticket transcripts + metadata mapping doc.
- Build a Redwood endpoint: small private deployment with dedicated capacity for pilot hours.
- Demo day: compare baseline vs Redwood outputs on 100 held-out tickets (AHT proxy and token cost).
- Deliverable: short deck with AHT estimate, token-cost delta, recommended rollout plan.

Objection handling (script snippets):
- "We already use X LLM vendor." -> "Totally — many teams do. Quick way to evaluate: a side-by-side on 100 tickets focusing on cost per resolved ticket and latency. Redwood's strength is predictable unit economics once you move to steady state (dedicated pools + batching/cache)."
- "Security/compliance concerns." -> "We can run a Private deployment in your VPC and integrate with your KMS; for pilot we can work with anonymized/test data and provide audit logs."
- "We don't want vendor lock-in." -> "Redwood supports multiple model variants and makes rollouts model-agnostic; customers switch models without changing the API contract — reduces lock-in risk."
- "What's the ROI?" -> "We estimate 20–30% reduction in AHT for templated inquiries. Rough math: X merchants * Y tickets/mo * AHT savings * avg USD per support hour => clear payback in 3–6 months at mid-market pricing. Will validate in pilot."

Technical readiness checklist (for SRE convo):
- Does Vela require VPC-only endpoints? yes/no. If yes, discuss Private deployment + network peering.
- Peak QPS and P95 latency targets — can Redwood meet with dedicated pool sizing?
- Where to route fallbacks — route to smaller quantized model or to existing vendor?
- Data retention: logs retention window and where to store audit logs.
- Secrets/KMS: confirm KMS provider (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HashiCorp Vault).

Pricing talking points (shorthand to use in pitch):
- Pilot: fixed effort + small dedicated pool for 2 weeks (cap on tokens). Keep straightforward: flat pilot fee $X + committed capacity optional.
- Post-pilot: two paths — usage-based Hosted API (fast) or Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable unit economics.

Competitive notes (why Redwood):
- Compared to hyperscalers: better batching/kv cache for steady-state token cost; more transparent cost breakdowns per route.
- Compared to LLM-only startups: Redwood offers infra and rollout tooling (canary, A/B, automatic fallback) which matters in production.
- Risk: if Vela already has an internal infra team that prefers self-hosting, emphasize partnership (Private + professional services).

Open questions / homework (next actions):
- Ask Marcel to pull a sample dataset schema from Vela POC contact (what fields, examples).
- Get a rough ticket volume estimate and average token size — Liam to ask during intro.
- Draft a 1-page pilot contract + data processing addendum (send to legal for template).
- Prepare a 15-min technical appendix demo showing latency and fallback examples.

Meeting prep checklist: (15-min intro)
- 1-slide: quick company + use cases (support, fraud, reconciliation)
- 1-slide: pilot ask and timeline
- 1-slide: security & compliance (Private options, KMS, audit logs)
- 1-slide: expected outcomes + next steps

Reminders (notes-to-self):
- Keep initial outreach focused on merchant support ops ; technical hooks are secondary.
- Avoid heavy pricing in first email — aim to get a meeting.
- If they ask for references, use two mid-market PSP case studies (anonymized).

Possible subject lines to A/B test:
- "Cut merchant support time by 25% — quick pilot?"
- "Proof: 38% fewer tokens per dispute case (pilot offer)"
- "Vela + Redwood: low-lift pilot for support automation"

End of scratchpad.

-- Priya
